stem: In a school garden in Jaipur, Meera plants many sunflower saplings close together. After some weeks, the plants stay small and none of them grows too tall or spreads too much. Her teacher says this competition helps keep the garden balanced. Why does competition help maintain balance in this garden?

options.text: The plants stop using water and sunlight completely, so nothing in the garden changes.
Competition for shared sunlight, water and space limits the growth of each plant, so no single plant uses up all the resources.
Competition makes each plant grow faster, so all the plants become very large together.
Competition removes all the weaker plants, so the garden soon has no plants left at all.

teacher.key_rationale: Competition for shared limited resources (sunlight, water, space) restricts each plant's growth and resource use, preventing any one plant from dominating, which keeps the garden ecosystem balanced. A, C and D misstate the effect of competition.
